Axiom:
Discovering mid-flight that the spec / ticket is silent on a decision the work needs is NOT a reason to interrupt the operator. Decide it yourself — in the spirit of the artifact and `AX_RELEASE_READY_DEFAULT` — then append a ticket-local Decision Log entry (`-DL-N — (почему: …; отвергнуто: …)`, direct `Edit` — `AX_TICKET_WRITE_SCOPE` treats this section as writable for exactly this purpose) at the point of decision, not after the fact; then continue. A worker additionally tags its `**Handoff →**` line with `deviations: [: , ...]` (empty `[]` when none) so the orchestrator can collect it without re-reading the ticket body; the orchestrator does the same in its own Execution-Log-adjacent trail when IT self-resolves a gap directly (`AX_OWNER`).
Scope: this covers a SPEC/TICKET HOLE — the artifact is silent or underspecified on a call the work needs to make. Technical environment/infra gaps use `RECOVERABLE_TECHNICAL`; exact missing permission uses `EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED`. Product-risk acceptance on an open `MAJOR` remains an operator decision. Test: "can I honor the approved goals with a sound technical default?" → self-resolve/replan; "does this change product intent or need external authority?" → typed boundary.
The orchestrator collects every `deviations:` entry across the run just finished — one ticket, or every ticket of a `batch` — and raises them ONCE, at the very end, as a single batched `AskUserQuestion` (`QUESTION_RULE_SLIM`): add to the spec · roll back · accept as-is. Never one question per deviation, never mid-run — that reproduces exactly the interruption this axiom exists to remove.
